title: SIEM/webhook audit delivery: at-least-once guarantees, DLQ & batching
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers using Private/Dedicated deployments require robust delivery of audit events to external SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog) and custom webhooks. Current best-effort delivery occasionally drops events during transient downstream failures and maintenance windows. We need an at-least-once delivery mode that balances throughput and latency while providing observability, backpressure handling, and a developer-friendly DLQ for manual reconciliation.

Goal: Implement a pluggable delivery subsystem for audit events that: 1) guarantees at-least-once delivery to configured endpoints (Splunk HEC, Datadog Events API, generic webhooks), 2) supports configurable batching and ordering semantics per-organization, 3) exposes retry/backoff/DLQ controls in Console and API, and 4) provides tracing & metrics for delivered/failed/acked events so SREs and customers can investigate delivery health.
acceptance_criteria: At-least-once delivery path implemented for Splunk HEC and Datadog Events (config toggle per-tenant)
Persistent durable queue persists events across service restarts for Dedicated/Private (configurable retention window)
Configurable batching and max-latency window (defaults: 50ms or 100 events)
Per-tenant deduplication idempotency using monotonic sequence + stable event-id to avoid accidental duplication in downstream systems
Dead-letter queue (DLQ) that surfaces failed delivery batches in Console with retry and redrive actions
Delivery metrics and traces visible in Console: success rate, retry count histogram, p95 delivery latency, current queue backlog
Test harness that fuzzes downstream 5xx, circuit-breakers, and simulates network partitions; audits are preserved and either redelivered or moved to DLQ
work_items: Design: delivery protocol and idempotency headers for Splunk/Datadog/webhook (RFC)
Engine: implement persistent queue (RocksDB-backed) + in-memory index for dedupe
Engine: batcher worker with configurable batch size/time and exponential backoff with jitter
Engine: ack protocol and idempotency key generation (per-event UUID + sequence per-org)
API: endpoints for tenant delivery settings, DLQ inspection, manual redrive
Console: UI for delivery health, per-tenant backlog, and DLQ action buttons
E2E tests: local integration tests with Splunk HEC mock and Datadog mock
Runbook: operational playbook for large backlog or stuck delivery workers
comments: 2026-03-10 Arielle Chen: Created ticket after postmortem from 2026-03-02 incident where 1.3% of audit events were lost during a rolling deploy. Proposed a durable queue + DLQ + per-tenant flags for at-least-once.

2026-03-11 Miguel Torres: Spike completed — implemented prototype RocksDB-backed queue and a simple batcher. Observed ~12% CPU overhead at 1k eps with default batch settings. Adding variant with Redis stream benchmark next.

2026-03-12 Design review (Dalia Park): Recommended idempotency header format 'X-Redwood-Audit-Id' + sequence 'X-Redwood-Audit-Seq' and per-tenant sequence checkpoint stored in KV. Raised concern about ordering guarantees across multi-worker sharding; suggested per-tenant single-shard ordering with parallel workers for different org partitions.

2026-03-13 Security review (Carlos Mendes): Approved approach for at-least-once but flagged KMS usage for DLQ replays in Private deployments; customer-managed KMS keys must be supported. Action: add KMS integration task.

2026-03-14 Miguel Torres: Implemented DLQ API and Console stub. Added test harness that simulates downstream 503s with 95% success after retries. Found edge case where duplicate retries created out-of-order sequences in customer dashboards; adding sequence check in consumer adapter.
